parsed.attack: Name the recipient of the exported house sheet and the loop stalls: a contractor does not want his customer's app, he wants the part number the PDF already gave him free, and a house buyer receives it once at a sale that happens roughly once a decade. The founder's own kill line sets the bar at 5% of exported sheets being opened by a second person within 90 days, which is an admission that the artifact usually never leaves the phone, and when it does the cycle time is measured in years rather than the days a working loop needs. A $25 one-time price then forecloses the fallback, because there is no recurring revenue to fund a referral incentive and paid acquisition costs $20-$80 per payer against a $25 gross ticket.
parsed.strongest_defence: Rural first-time owners concentrate in free high-intent places - r/homeowners, well-and-septic groups, homesteading YouTube - and the unit that actually travels is not the formal export but a screenshot of 'my pump switch, identified, with the part that fits', posted into a thread where someone has just asked exactly that question, which converts because the reader is standing in the same crawlspace.
parsed.verdict_reason: The claimed shareable artifact goes to recipients with no reason to install, at decade-scale events, leaving slow unpaid forum word of mouth as the real channel.
